Method of Attack: The attacker built up a credible reputation as an OSS developer over the span of multiple years and used highly obfuscated code in order to evade detection by code reviews. The malicious payload ran in the same process as the OpenSSH server (SSHD) and modified decryption routines in the OpenSSH server in order to allow specific remote attackers to send arbitrary payloads through SSH which will be executed before the authentication step, effectively hijacking the entire victim machine.
Indicators of Compromise: The malicious code enables unauthorized remote SSH access and modifies decryption routines in the OpenSSH server in order to allow specific remote attackers to send arbitrary payloads through SSH which will be executed before the authentication step.
